paragraphs.en: Higher life expectancy ( (预期寿命) ) means an increased {duration} of our lives.Even if we're healthy, {wrinkles} around the {forehead} show that we're {aging} .The heart ages, too.It is no longer as {efficient} in processing {oxygen} as it {used} {to} be.In most people, the first {signs} show up in their 50s or early 60s, as they enter their later years and {retire} .And among people who don't exercise, the changes can start even sooner.
paragraphs.cn: 预期寿命的延长意味着我们生命的 <u> 持续时间 </u> 延长。即使我们身体健康， <u> 额头 </u> 上的 <u> 皱纹 </u> 也会表明我们正在 <u> 衰老 </u> 。心脏也会衰老。它在处理 <u> 氧气 </u> 方面不再像 <u> 以前 </u> 那样 <u> 高效 </u> 了。对于大多数人来说，当他们步入老年并 <u> 退休 </u> 时，也就是50多岁或60岁出头时，这些衰老 <u> 迹象 </u> 就会开始出现。而在不锻炼的人群中，这种变化可能开始得更早。

paragraphs.en: "Think of a {rubber} {band} .In the beginning, it is flexible, but put it in a {drawer} for 20 years, and it will become {dry} and easily broken,"says Dr.Ben Levine, a heart {specialist} at the University of Texas.That's what happens to the heart.Changes in the heart's structure at the {millimeter} level can lead to a variety of issues. {Fortunately} for those in {midlife} , Levine is finding that even if you haven't been an enthusiastic exerciser, getting in shape now may help improve your {aging} heart.
paragraphs.cn: 得克萨斯大学的心脏 <u> 专家 </u> 本·莱文博士说："想象一根 <u> 橡皮筋 </u> 。一开始，它很有弹性，但把它放在 <u> 抽屉 </u> 里20年后，它会变 <u> 干 </u> 且容易断裂。"心脏也是如此。心脏结构中 <u> 毫米 </u> 级别的变化就会导致各种问题。 <u> 幸运的是 </u> ，莱文发现，对于那些处于 <u> 中年 </u> 的人群来说，即使你过去不是一个热衷锻炼的人，现在开始锻炼也会有助于改善你 <u> 逐渐衰老的 </u> 心脏。

paragraphs.en: Levine and his research team {selected} {volunteers} {aged} between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy.Participants were {randomly} divided into two groups.The first group {participated} in a program of nonaerobic ( (无氧) ) exercise—balance {training} and weight training—three times a week.The second group did high-intensity ( (高强度) ) aerobic exercise {under} the {guidance} of a {trainer} for four or more days a week.After two years, the second group saw {remarkable} {improvements} in heart health.
paragraphs.cn: 莱文和他的研究小组 <u> 挑选 </u> 了 <u> 年龄 </u> 在45至64岁之间、平时锻炼不多但身体健康的 <u> 志愿者 </u> 。这些参与者被 <u> 随机 </u> 分为两组。第一组每周 <u> 参加 </u> 三次无氧运动的训练项目——平衡 <u> 训练 </u> 和负重训练。第二组在 <u> 教练 </u> 的 <u> 指导下 </u> ，每周进行四天或四天以上高强度的有氧运动。两年后，第二组的心脏健康状况有了 <u> 显著改善 </u> 。

paragraphs.en: "We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30-or 35-year-old hearts,"says Levine."And the reason they got so much stronger and fitter was that their hearts could now fill with blood a lot better and pump ( (泵送) ) a lot more {blood} during exercise."But the hearts of those who participated in less {intense} exercise didn't change, he says.
paragraphs.cn: 莱文说："我们研究了这些50岁的心脏，并让它们回到了30岁或35岁时的心脏状态。他们之所以变得更强壮、更健康，是因为在运动时，他们的心脏能够更好地充盈血液，并泵送出更多的 <u> 血液 </u> 。"但他表示，那些参加低 <u> 强度 </u> 运动的人，心脏并没有发生变化。

paragraphs.en: "The {sweet} spot in life to start exercising, if you haven't {already} , is in late middle age when the heart still has {flexibility} ,"Levine says."We put healthy 70-year-olds through a {yearlong} exercise training program, and {nothing} happened to them at all."
paragraphs.cn: 莱文说："如果你还没有开始锻炼，那么人生中开始锻炼的 <u> 最佳 </u> 时机是在中年后期，此时的心脏仍具有 <u> 弹性 </u> 。我们让健康的70岁老人参加了 <u> 为期一年的 </u> 运动训练项目，结果他们身上 <u> 没有任何 </u> 变化。"

paragraphs.en: The implication is that if you are not already a {keen} exerciser, you should consider a {jog} on {Monday} morning or activities like {boxing} and {swimming} from now on.Set a {monthly} exercise routine if necessary.These exercises stimulate the heart to pump more efficiently, which may also help reduce the strain on your {shoulder} and {neck} muscles.
paragraphs.cn: 这意味着，如果你不是一个 <u> 热衷 </u> 锻炼的人，那么从现在开始，你应该考虑在 <u> 周一 </u> 早上 <u> 慢跑 </u> ，或者参加 <u> 拳击 </u> 、 <u> 游泳 </u> 等活动。如有必要，可以制定 <u> 月度 </u> 锻炼计划。这些运动能刺激心脏更高效地泵送血液，还可能有助于减轻 <u> 肩颈 </u> 肌肉的压力。

paragraphs.en: Dr.Nieca Goldberg, a {spokeswoman} for the American Heart {Association} , says Levine's {findings} are a great start.But the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference.
paragraphs.cn: 美国心脏 <u> 协会发言人 </u> 尼卡·戈德堡博士说，莱文的 <u> 发现 </u> 是一个很好的开始。但这项研究的样本量较小，需要在更大规模的人群中重复进行，以准确地确定日常锻炼的哪些方面能产生最大的影响。
